overall_reason: The page is built from the visitor's own questions (Do I still have to chase? What does my client receive? What if they write back? When does the chasing stop? What does it cost?) and answers each with the product in a telling state, with figures that reconcile across every mock; the surface (heavy grotesk, warm near-white, one salmon accent, pills everywhere, giant footer wordmark) is the generic part.

findings.evidence: T-MIRROR on the surface only: tight heavy grotesk display, warm near-white ground (oklch 0.97 0.006 55), a single salmon/red accent, every button and status as a pill (Sign up, Start for £8 a month, See a reminder, All/Chasing/Paid chips, Sent/Paid badges) and an 8px-radius soft-shadow panel recipe on four figures (sweep card_kit). A neighbouring fintech brief would get the same skin. The display face was meant to be General Sans (blocked at capture), so the exact face was not judged.
findings.before: pill buttons + pill chips + pill badges, one accent, grotesk
findings.after: Keep pills for status badges only (where they mean state) and give buttons a different shape; take one cue from invoices themselves (ruled ledger lines, tabular figures already in Geist Mono) into the page chrome
findings.why: The content is specific; the skin is the product-chrome default (SLP-121 'pill buttons everywhere').

findings.where: #chase 'Do I still have to chase?' (1440 tile 01)
findings.evidence: Failed T-DELETION: the section is an h2, one sentence ('No. Tilly writes to the client while you get on with the work.') and a half-width library photo (blocked at capture; credited as 'Florist working', Wikimedia). The sentence restates the hero sub-line; removing the section loses only the photo. Sweep dead bands at y783-1020 and y1584-1765 sit either side of it.
findings.after: Merge the answer into the next section ('What does my client receive?') as its lead, or give this section the reminder schedule itself ([DATA NEEDED: default reminder cadence, e.g. days after due])
findings.why: A head and a paragraph are a head block, not a section; the page's one thin screen.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DELETION: the footer opens with the wordmark at 240px, the largest type on the page, carrying no information; the giant footer wordmark is a current template habit. The nav already names the product twice.
findings.after: Drop to the nav wordmark size, or use the space for one fact (who makes it, where, support contact [DATA NEEDED])
findings.why: Scale spent on decoration at the end of the page.

findings.evidence: The page's only photograph is a Wikimedia library frame ('Florist_working.jpg', direct2Florist, CC BY 2.0) in a 752px-wide slot beside 'Do I still have to chase?'. It shows a generic freelancer at work, not the product or a Tilly user.
findings.before: library photo of a florist in a half-width slot
findings.after: Use the slot for the product (the reminder schedule or the 'Chasing' row) or shrink the photo to a detail slot (IMG-132); credit already present
findings.why: Mood stock in a major slot on a page that otherwise shows its product everywhere.

strengths: Question-led structure that follows a freelancer's real hesitations, ending on price: 'What does it cost? £8 a month.' This is the page's idea; keep it.

The product is shown in telling states, and the data reconciles: outstanding £4,520.00 equals 0045 + 0044 + 0043 + 0042; invoice 0042 lines £300.00 + £80.00 = £380.00, due 2 Oct, and 'now 7 days overdue' matches 'Reminder 2 Today, 09:00'; invoice 0041's timeline (sent 12 Sep, due 26 Sep, reply 30 Sep 'Paying this week.', paid 3 Oct) matches the inbox and hero ledger.
The h1 'Never write “following up” again.' names the exact chore with hung punctuation; the CTA carries the price ('Start for £8 a month').
Honest form: unconnected signup reports 'Nothing was sent: this form is not connected yet.' Phone layout is rebuilt, not shrunk (375 tile 00).
